repository.name: webpack

issue.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template because we'll close your issue -->

# Bug report

<!-- Please ask questions on StackOverflow or the webpack Gitter. -->
<!-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask?tags=webpack -->
<!-- https://gitter.im/webpack/webpack -->
<!-- Issues which contain questions or support requests will be closed. -->

**What is the current behavior?**
When I compile in a production environment, I found that global css cannot be output, only css of css-modules can be output. This appeared in the webpack 5.1.1 version. When I used webpack 5.1.0, this problem did not occur.

For example, what should be output is:
```css
.app {
  color: #000;
}

._1NBoggxDtp1TrWNgYFXOtj {
  color: #f00;
}
```
But actually the output is:

```css
._1NBoggxDtp1TrWNgYFXOtj {
  color: #f00;
}
```

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**
Demo: [https://github.com/duan602728596/webpack-bug-demo](https://github.com/duan602728596/webpack-bug-demo)

<!-- A great way to do this is to provide your configuration via a GitHub repository -->
<!-- The most helpful is a minimal reproduction with instructions on how to reproduce -->
<!-- Repositories with too many files or large `webpack.config.js` files are not suitable -->
<!-- Please only add small code snippets directly into this issue -->
<!-- https://gist.github.com is a good place for longer code snippets -->
<!-- If your issue is caused by a plugin or loader, please create an issue on the loader/plugin repository instead -->

**What is the expected behavior?**
The css file should contain css-modules css and global css.

<!-- "It should work" is not a helpful explanation -->
<!-- Explain exactly how it should behave -->

**Other relevant information:**
webpack version: 5.1.1
Node.js version: 14.9.0
Operating System: macOS 10.15.6
Additional tools: yarn@1.22.5

body: Thanks for issue, keep using webpack@5.1.0, fix will be soon

body:
Seems like this case slipped through the process. I think our test suite still runs against an older version of mini-css.

I revert the change until I find a better fix tomorrow.

Thanks for the quick response! The issue is not present any more in 5.1.2.
Also, I've tested @sokra's assumption, and indeed the tests are running against an older version of mini-css. If I bump it to the latest version, [the tests that cover the mini-css-extract-plugin](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/tree/master/test/watchCases/plugins/mini-css-extract-plugin) indeed start to fail.
